paper_title: Axion and neutrino bounds improved with new calibrations of the tip of the red-giant branch using geometric distance determinations
notes: TRGB stellar-energy-loss bound on the axion-electron coupling g_ae (dimensionless, standard g_ae = C_e m_e/f_a convention; paper writes g_13 = g_ae x 10^13). Value taken from the abstract and Table I. The paper reports several targets: NGC 4258 (cleanest extra-galactic) g_ae < 1.6e-13 (95% CL), LMC g_ae < 1.58e-13, and omega Centauri (best galactic target) g_ae < 1.3e-13 (95% CL). Reported here is the strongest (omega Cen, g_13 = 1.29 at 95% CL) since that defines the boundary of the excluded region; the abstract's primary extra-galactic value NGC 4258 gives 1.6e-13 (within a factor of ~1.2). This is a stellar-cooling bound valid for light axions (m_a << stellar core temperature ~10 keV), so it is a mass-independent flat line; the mass range shown (1e-9 to 1e4 eV) is nominal, not stated by the paper. Not a dark-matter search, so no density assumption. Corresponding neutrino magnetic-moment bounds are also given but out of scope.
